newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti picks De Benedetti man for top job.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti picks De Benedetti man for top job.

text.p: Roberto Colaninno, the new man at the helm of struggling loss-making Olivetti, is a close business associate of former chairman Carlo De Benedetti, who helped Colaninno establish his own auto components group.
Colaninno, 53, also has banking experience as a member of the board of Italian local banking groups Banca Agricola Mantovana and Banca Steinhauslin.

He was appointed the new chief executive of Olivetti after a group extraordinary board meeting late on Wednesday, replacing the 39-year old Francesco Caio after only 76 days at the head of the crisis-hit information technology group.
Colaninno started his career with auto components group FIAAM, working abroad particularly in the United States before rising to become group managing director.
The firm was taken over in 1978 by British groups Ferodo and Coopers, and three years later Colaninno founded his own auto components group Sogefi in the northern Italian city of Mantova.

De Benedetti took a controlling stake in the company through his family holding group CIR with the object of creating a major Italian group in the auto components sector and eventually listing the company's shares on the Milan bourse.
After 14 years, the Sogefi had a 1995 turnover of 920 billion lire ($602.5 million) and made a profit of 34 billion lire. It has 4,500 employees across eleven countries. ($1=1527 Lire)
